name: table-search
title: TableSearch
description: Controlled table-search editor with slash-invoked field scoping, removable inset field Chips, and an input-focused listbox keyboard model.

intent.summary: Controlled table-search editor with slash-invoked field scoping, removable inset field Chips, and an input-focused listbox keyboard model.
useWhen: A data-table search needs optional field-specific scopes without replacing the application's filtering logic.
People should be able to add one or more searchable data points through a slash command while continuing to type one free-text query.
avoidWhen: A plain global text search is sufficient; use Input with type search.
The choices are persistent filters with independent values; use TableFilter or Select instead.
The component is expected to inspect records, build a search index, or filter rows internally.
accessibility: The native search input remains the one Tab stop and exposes combobox, expanded, controls, and active-descendant relationships to the field listbox.

Typing slash opens the field listbox without inserting slash into the query. While open, Up and Down change the active option, Enter selects it, Escape or Backspace closes it, and Left and Right retain native text-cursor behavior because focus never leaves the input.
The query disables browser autocomplete history, automatic capitalization, autocorrection, and spellchecking so browser-owned suggestions never obscure the product-owned field menu or table results.

Selected field Chips have individually labeled remove actions and are also described by the search input. Polite announcements report additions, removals, and clearing without duplicating the visible query.
The slash suffix is a labeled double-inset md button excluded from sequential keyboard navigation; the search input exposes the same action through aria-keyshortcuts and its description.
The clear action removes both free text and every selected field. It restores focus to the search input; each Chip's own remove action remains scoped to that field.
states: value and selectedFieldIds are controlled. columns supplies the same table catalog used by Table and TableSort; dataLabel provides the complete out-of-context name while header and header segment label may remain compact. dsChange reports query edits, dsFieldsChange reports the next ordered field identities, and dsClear reports a complete clear. The component never filters rows or mutates consumer inputs.
The field menu excludes already-selected identities and closes after one selection. Typing slash again reopens the remaining fields so multiple scopes can be added.
Selected scopes render as neutral md Chips using the double-inset recipe so they remain 24px high inside the 32px md search control and each can be removed directly.

Backspace first closes an open slash listbox without editing query text or removing a field. When query text is empty and the listbox is already closed, the next Backspace removes the last selected field. Ordinary Backspace edits query text when the listbox is closed.
Duplicate, blank, and unknown field identities are ignored for presentation. Selected fields preserve the consumer's order.
Inactive search leaves the tab order, closes the field listbox, and does not emit query or field changes.
responsiveBehavior: The control fills the available inline size supplied by the table toolbar search slot. Selected Chips and the editable query share one horizontal editor lane so the md control does not grow vertically.

The field popup enters the top layer, aligns its first choice cell with the search control, flips or clamps to the viewport or nearest overlay boundary, and scrolls internally when its catalog is taller than available space.

Long selected field labels truncate inside their Chips while the input remains available at the inline end of the editor lane. Both suffix actions resolve to the same 24px height as selected Chips. Clear follows the standard md Input recipe—a non-inset sm icon button—while slash is a double-inset md label button. Slash remains rightmost; when query text exposes Clear, a vertical divider separates the two actions.

customElements: Assign columns and selectedFieldIds through JavaScript properties and replace controlled values from dsChange and dsFieldsChange.
Keep field IDs aligned with the application search index; the component treats IDs as opaque values.
react: Pass new array references for columns and selectedFieldIds and update controlled state from onDsChange and onDsFieldsChange.
angular: Import DsTableSearch, bind columns, selectedFieldIds, and value, then update application signals from dsChange and dsFieldsChange.

columns.description: Table column catalog used to derive searchable data points and their complete labels.

selectedFieldIds.description: Controlled ordered field scopes rendered as Tags.
